title: No Communication Between Control Board And Display
shortDescription: The thermostat or control panel has lost communication with the main control board.
fullDescription:
Dometic RV refrigerators and air conditioners communicate over a serial data line between the user display/thermostat and the main control board. When that link drops, the display shows NO CO (no communication) and refuses to operate. Common on Penguin II AC units and RM-series fridges.

Typical causes are a loose or corroded data cable, a blown fuse on the board, or a failed display. On rooftop AC units the cable runs from the ceiling assembly through the roof duct, and chafing is common. On fridges the board is behind the lower exterior vent.

Turn off 12V and shore power before inspecting the harness to avoid backfeed through the inverter.

causes.cause: Loose or disconnected data ribbon / 4-wire cable
Blown 3A fuse on main control board

fixSteps.title: Cycle power
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect shore power and 12V battery for 5 minutes, then reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Reseat data cable
fixSteps.instruction: Access the control board and reseat both ends of the communication harness.

fixSteps.title: Check fuses
fixSteps.instruction: Test the 3A board fuse with a multimeter; replace if open.

whenToCallPro: If reseating cables and replacing fuses does not restore communication, the control board likely needs replacement by an RV tech.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic RV NO CO error fix

faq.q: Can I still run the fridge on propane?
faq.a: No — the control board manages both gas and electric operation, so NO CO disables all modes.

title: No Power / Unit Not Receiving 12V
shortDescription: The appliance reports zero power or the display is blank due to a 12V DC supply fault.
fullDescription:
Dometic RV appliances require a steady 12V DC supply for the control board even when running on propane or 120V AC. A '0' reading or completely dark display indicates the DC side is dead.

Check the house battery voltage first (should be 12.4V+), then the 12V fuse at the converter/distribution panel, and finally the wiring to the unit.

Do not bypass fuses — a short in RV wiring can ignite propane vapors near the fridge vent.

causes.cause: Loose DC wire at appliance terminal block

fixSteps.title: Test battery voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter at the house battery — should read 12.4-13.6V.

fixSteps.title: Check DC fuse panel
fixSteps.instruction: Locate and test the fridge/AC fuse; replace if blown.

fixSteps.title: Verify voltage at unit
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm 12V present at the appliance DC terminal block.

whenToCallPro: If 12V is present at the unit but the display stays at 0, the control board is suspect — have a tech confirm before replacing.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic RV fridge no power 0 fix

faq.q: Why does my fridge lose power when I unplug shore power?
faq.a: The converter stops charging, so a weak house battery drops below the 10.5V cutoff.

title: Gas Valve / Burner Ignition Failure
shortDescription: The fridge attempted to ignite on propane and failed to detect flame after three tries.
fullDescription:
Code 2 on Dometic absorption refrigerators indicates the module tried to light the burner, did not sense flame within the trial period, and locked out. The boiler section will not cool until reset.

Common causes are low propane pressure, a dirty burner orifice, a cracked ceramic igniter/sensor, or spider webs in the flue (very common after storage).

Turn off the propane tank before removing the burner access cover. Check for gas smell before retrying.

causes.cause: Dirty burner orifice or spider webs in flue

symptoms: No click or spark at burner

fixSteps.title: Verify propane supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm tank is open and other propane appliances light normally.

fixSteps.title: Clean burner and orifice
fixSteps.instruction: Remove burner, blow out with compressed air, clear any webs from flue tube.

fixSteps.title: Check electrode gap
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect igniter for cracks; gap should be ~1/8 inch from burner.

whenToCallPro: If you smell gas or the solenoid valve is suspect — leaking propane is a fire hazard.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic RV fridge error code 2 no flame

faq.q: Why does this happen after storage?
faq.a: Mud daubers and spiders love the warm flue tube and build webs that block the burner airflow.

title: AC Heating Element Failure
shortDescription: The 120V AC heating element has failed or has no voltage.
fullDescription:
Code 3 indicates the fridge cannot heat the boiler on shore power. The board checks element resistance and current draw; if out of range, it flags the element circuit.

The element is a cartridge-type heater inserted into the boiler pocket. Normal resistance is 40-60 ohms. An open element reads OL.

Disconnect 120V at the breaker before testing to avoid shock — the element sits behind the lower exterior vent.

causes.cause: Tripped thermal fuse in element circuit
Failed AC relay on control board

symptoms: Fridge works on gas but not electric
No warmth at boiler on AC mode

fixSteps.title: Disconnect 120V
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the fridge breaker and unplug shore power.

fixSteps.title: Test element resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect element leads and measure resistance — 40-60 ohms is good, OL means replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace element
fixSteps.instruction: Pull old cartridge from boiler pocket and install new one with thermal paste.

whenToCallPro: If element tests good and fault persists, the control board AC relay is failing — tech replacement recommended.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic fridge error 3 heating element replace

faq.q: Can I run the fridge on propane only until I fix this?
faq.a: Yes — gas mode is independent of the AC element circuit.

title: Boiler Thermistor Out Of Range
shortDescription: The freezer or boiler temperature sensor is reading outside acceptable limits.
fullDescription:
Dometic fridges use a thermistor clipped to the freezer fins or boiler tube. Code 4 means the resistance is infinite (open) or near zero (shorted).

Normal resistance at room temperature is about 10k ohms. A pinched wire from the fridge rack can sever the thermistor lead.

This is a low-voltage sensor — no shock risk, but lift the wires carefully from inside the freezer.
symptoms: Fridge runs too cold or too warm

fixSteps.title: Inspect thermistor clip
fixSteps.instruction: Check that the bead sensor is clipped to the correct fin inside the fridge box.

fixSteps.title: Measure resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect at the board and measure ~10k ohms at room temperature.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in a new sensor and route wires away from racks.

whenToCallPro: If resistance reads correctly but fault persists, the control board is suspect.

faq.q: Does fridge temperature setting affect this code?
faq.a: No — the code reflects sensor hardware, not setpoint.

title: Cooling Unit Overheat / Boiler Temperature High
shortDescription: The boiler thermal sensor has detected excessive temperature, shutting the fridge down.
fullDescription:
Code 5 is a safety lockout — the boiler has exceeded ~400°F, which points to a failed cooling unit or prolonged off-level operation. Running a Dometic absorption fridge more than 3° off-level damages the cooling loop.

The thermal sensor (high-limit) is on the boiler jacket. Once tripped, some models auto-reset after cooldown; others require a hard reset.

Do not override the thermal fuse — an overheated cooling unit can release ammonia and catch fire.

causes.cause: RV parked off-level for extended period
Failed cooling unit (yellow residue on boiler)

symptoms: Yellow powder or ammonia smell behind fridge

fixSteps.title: Level the RV
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the coach is level within 3° before retrying.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cooling unit
fixSteps.instruction: Look for yellow/green residue on the boiler — indicates leaked cooling fluid.

fixSteps.title: Clear flue
fixSteps.instruction: Remove flue baffle and clean any obstructions.

whenToCallPro: Yellow residue means the cooling unit is ruptured — professional replacement or full fridge swap is needed.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic RV fridge error 5 cooling unit

faq.q: Is a leaked cooling unit dangerous?
faq.a: Ammonia fumes are toxic and flammable — ventilate immediately and stop using the fridge.

title: General Check Light Indicator
shortDescription: Fridge has detected a fault and requires manual reset.
fullDescription:
The CHECK LED on older Dometic RM-series fridges lights when any fault occurs — gas ignition failure, low battery, or thermistor issues. Newer models use numeric codes instead.

Press the ON/OFF button to reset after correcting the underlying issue. If it relights immediately, the fault is still present.

Always diagnose the root cause before repeatedly resetting.

fixSteps.title: Reset unit
fixSteps.instruction: Press ON/OFF to clear, then verify mode.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose cause
fixSteps.instruction: Check propane, DC voltage, and burner cleanliness.

whenToCallPro: If CHECK re-trips immediately after multiple resets and propane/battery are good.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic RV fridge check light reset

faq.q: Can I keep resetting the check light?
faq.a: Resetting masks a real problem — diagnose and repair instead.

title: Rooftop AC Evaporator Iced Over
shortDescription: The rooftop AC evaporator coil has frozen due to low airflow or low refrigerant.
fullDescription:
Penguin II and Brisk II rooftop AC units ice up when airflow is restricted or outdoor temps drop below 60°F at high fan settings. A freeze sensor stops the compressor to protect it.

Clean the return air filter and inspect the ceiling assembly gasket for leaks. Running AC with windows open in cool weather is a common cause.

Let the coil thaw fully (at least 30 min) before restarting; otherwise the sensor retrips immediately.

causes.cause: Outdoor temperature too low for cooling

fixSteps.title: Switch off AC and thaw
fixSteps.instruction: Turn AC off, run fan only for 30 minutes until ice melts.

fixSteps.title: Clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Wash or replace return air filter.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil
fixSteps.instruction: Remove ceiling assembly and vacuum evap fins.

whenToCallPro: If icing persists after cleaning, refrigerant is likely low — requires certified HVAC service.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic Penguin II AC frozen coil fix

faq.q: Why does my RV AC freeze on cool nights?
faq.a: Below 60°F outdoor, the coil can't shed heat and ices up — use fan only instead.

title: Power Awning Motor Stalled
shortDescription: The awning motor overloaded or cannot complete travel.
fullDescription:
Dometic power awnings use a 12V motor with a thermal overload. If the awning binds, the fabric is wrapped tight, or wind pressure is excessive, the motor stalls and the controller cuts power for 30 seconds.

Clear the obstruction, let the motor cool, then retry. Repeated stalls indicate worn gears or a torsion spring failure.

Never reach into a partially retracted awning — sudden motor recovery can pinch fingers.

causes.cause: Awning fabric bound or dirty roller

fixSteps.title: Release pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Wait 30 seconds for thermal reset and retry.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fabric
fixSteps.instruction: Check for jams, twisted fabric, or debris in the roller.

fixSteps.title: Measure battery under load
fixSteps.instruction: Voltage should stay above 11.5V during motor run.

whenToCallPro: If motor is confirmed failed or torsion spring is broken — spring tension can cause injury.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic power awning motor stall fix

faq.q: How windy is too windy for a power awning?
faq.a: Most Dometic awnings rate 20 mph max — retract in any sustained gusts.

title: Electric Toilet Flush Motor Failure
shortDescription: The motorized flush ball or pedal actuator will not cycle.
fullDescription:
Dometic 310/320 series electric toilets use a 12V motor to rotate the flush ball. If the motor jams on debris, loses power, or the switch fails, the bowl will not clear.

Check the inline fuse first, then the foot switch wiring, then the motor. A common cause is calcium buildup around the ball seal.

Close the water supply before disassembly to avoid flooding.

causes.cause: Jammed flush ball from debris or scale

symptoms: No motor sound when pedal pressed

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Locate toilet circuit fuse at DC panel and test.

fixSteps.title: Clear debris
fixSteps.instruction: Close water, open ball manually, remove any solid matter.

fixSteps.title: Test pedal switch
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity when pedal is pressed.

whenToCallPro: If the ball seal is broken and the tank backflows, replacement is messy — a tech may be preferable.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic 310 RV toilet flush motor replace

faq.q: Why doesn't my toilet hold water in the bowl?
faq.a: The ball seal is worn — replace the rubber seal kit.

title: AC High-Pressure Switch Tripped
shortDescription: The rooftop AC high-pressure safety cut out.
fullDescription:
P1 on Dometic Penguin II / Blizzard units indicates the high-side refrigerant pressure exceeded the safety threshold. The compressor shuts down to prevent damage.

Most common cause is a dirty condenser coil on the roof — dust and bugs block airflow. Clean the coil with a garden hose (fins from inside out) on a cool day.

High-pressure faults can indicate overcharge — do not add refrigerant without proper gauges and certification.

fixSteps.title: Power off and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off AC breaker, climb roof, remove shroud.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Spray fins gently with water, avoid bending them.

fixSteps.title: Test fan operation
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm condenser fan spins freely and at full speed.

whenToCallPro: If condenser is clean but P1 persists — refrigerant system issue requires EPA-certified technician.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic RV AC P1 high pressure fix

faq.q: Is it safe to climb my RV roof?
faq.a: Only if the roof is rated for walking — check owner's manual first.

title: AC Low-Pressure / Refrigerant Loss
shortDescription: The AC sensed low refrigerant pressure and shut down.
fullDescription:
P2 indicates the low-side pressure fell below threshold — typically a refrigerant leak or cold ambient operation. The compressor locks out to prevent slugging.

Leaks usually occur at the Schrader valve, flare fittings, or a cracked evap coil. Only EPA 608-certified technicians can recharge the system.

Running a leaking AC worsens compressor wear — stop using the unit until repaired.

fixSteps.title: Verify ambient temp
fixSteps.instruction: Do not run AC below 60°F outside.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for oil residue
fixSteps.instruction: Oil on fittings or coil indicates refrigerant leak.

fixSteps.title: Call HVAC tech
fixSteps.instruction: Certified tech must locate leak and recharge.

whenToCallPro: Always — R410A refrigerant work requires EPA certification and proper gauges.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic RV AC P2 low pressure refrigerant

faq.a: No — it's illegal without EPA 608 certification and requires specialized tools.

title: Room Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The CCC2 thermostat room sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
E1 on the Dometic CCC2 comfort control indicates the room air sensor, located inside the thermostat housing, is out of range. The system cannot regulate temperature and defaults to fixed-time cycles.

Sensor is part of the thermostat assembly — replace as a unit. Check for condensation or insect debris inside the housing first.

causes.cause: Moisture or debris in thermostat housing

fixSteps.title: Remove thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: Pull thermostat off wall, inspect back cavity.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: If fault persists, install new CCC2 unit.

whenToCallPro: If new thermostat still shows E1, the main control board communication is likely faulty.

faq.q: Will my AC still work with E1?
faq.a: Partially — it runs on timed cycles but won't hit the target temperature accurately.

title: Outdoor Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The outdoor ambient sensor on the rooftop unit is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
Used on heat-pump-equipped Dometic rooftop units, the outdoor sensor sits on the condenser side and tells the system when to switch from heat pump to electric resistance heat. E2 means that sensor is faulty.

Access requires roof climb and shroud removal. Sensor is inexpensive but the location is the challenge.

fixSteps.title: Replace outdoor sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Unclip and swap in new thermistor.

whenToCallPro: If you are uncomfortable on the RV roof or the sensor harness is damaged back into the chassis.
videoSearchQuery: Dometic heat pump E2 outdoor sensor

faq.q: Can I still use heat with E2?
faq.a: Yes — electric heat strips still run, but efficiency drops.

title: Control Panel Locked
shortDescription: The child-lock or installer-lock is engaged and inputs are ignored.
fullDescription:
The CCC2 and newer Dometic controls have a child-lock that ignores button presses. LOCK on the display means keypad is disabled.

To unlock, press and hold MODE and FAN buttons simultaneously for 5 seconds. Some installer-locked systems require a dealer PIN.

fixSteps.title: Hold MODE + FAN
fixSteps.instruction: Press and hold both for 5 seconds to toggle lock.

whenToCallPro: Almost never — contact dealer only if an installer PIN was set.

faq.q: Why did my thermostat lock itself?
faq.a: Usually a kid or pet pressed the combo; it's a feature, not a fault.
